{
  "target_verification": {
    "building_identity": "high",
    "floor_identity": "high",
    "visual_relevance": "high",
    "verdict": "exact_match",
    "reason": "All key architectural identifiers match: 'Tiananmen Gate' is unambiguously named across multiple authoritative sources (China Daily, Wikipedia, Jianzhuzhichuang, 360Cities); structural identity (reconstructed 1651, post-1420 original) and formal typology (palace-style, not pavilion or gatehouse) are consistently confirmed; floor/level identity is explicitly stated as two-tiered (lower red brick city platform + upper timber-framed pavilion); visual features (red walls, multi-layered roof, dougong, latticed windows, balustrades, glazed tile roof, dragon-ornamented ridges) are repeatedly described and cross-verified."
  },
  "generation_module": "exterior_architecture",
  "scene_goal": "Generate a photorealistic exterior architectural visualization of Tiananmen Gate that accurately conveys its iconic volumetric composition, hierarchical roof structure, material hierarchy (vermilion walls, yellow glazed tiles), and ornamental grammar (dougong, latticed windows, stone栏杆, ridge beasts), prioritizing spatial legibility and atmospheric authenticity over metric precision.",
  "spaces": [
    {
      "name": "city platform",
      "type": "exterior",
      "confidence": "confirmed"
    },
    {
      "name": "upper pavilion",
      "type": "exterior",
      "confidence": "confirmed"
    },
    {
      "name": "roof ensemble",
      "type": "roof",
      "confidence": "confirmed"
    },
    {
      "name": "front facade",
      "type": "facade",
      "confidence": "confirmed"
    }
  ],
  "space_contracts": [
    {
      "space": "city platform",
      "boundary_mode": "closed",
      "floor": true,
      "walls": ["vermilion-painted brick masonry", "Hanbaiyu (white marble) base course", "Hanbaiyu balustrade with lotus-and-vase motifs"],
      "ceiling": false,
      "openings": ["five arched portals (central largest, flanked symmetrically)"],
      "connections": ["stair ramps (ma dao) on east/west sides", "connection to upper pavilion via interior stairs"],
      "vertical_geometry": ["13 m tall solid masonry mass", "1.59 m high carved Hanbaiyu xumizuo base"],
      "content_after_envelope": ["ground-level paving (stone slabs)", "outer Golden River bridge group (7 bridges, central imperial bridge)"]
    },
    {
      "space": "upper pavilion",
      "boundary_mode": "semi_open",
      "floor": true,
      "walls": ["vermilion-painted timber columns (60 total, 92 cm diameter)", "painted wooden lattice windows (36 front-facing, linghua pattern)", "painted wooden doors", "painted beam-and-bracket system (dougong + fang)"],
      "ceiling": true,
      "openings": ["36 linghua-pattern windows", "main entrance archway"],
      "connections": ["direct vertical access from city platform stairs", "roof assembly above"],
      "vertical_geometry": ["timber frame resting on platform", "elevation approx. 21.7 m above ground (34.7 m total height - 13 m platform)"],
      "content_after_envelope": ["external eaves, cornices, and decorative elements only — no interior furnishings or lighting fixtures"]
    },
    {
      "space": "roof ensemble",
      "boundary_mode": "open",
      "floor": false,
      "walls": [],
      "ceiling": true,
      "openings": [],
      "connections": ["attached to upper pavilion structure"],
      "vertical_geometry": ["double-eaved xieshan (hip-and-gable) roof", "nine-ridge configuration (1 main ridge + 8 hip/vertical ridges)", "yellow glazed ceramic tiles", "ten dragon-shaped吻 (chiwen) — 2 on main ridge, 8 on hip ridges", "zodiac animal procession on hip ridges (1 immortal + 9 beasts)"],
      "content_after_envelope": ["roof tile texture (interlocking convex-concave profile)", "ridge ornamentation scale and placement"]
    }
  ],
  "envelope_model": "assembled_elements_with_verified_joints",
  "hard_finish": {
    "required": ["wall_finish", "roof_finish", "balustrade_finish", "door_window_frame_finish", "threshold_or_sill", "readable_room_light"],
    "conditional": ["dougong_paint_pattern", "ridge_beast_material"],
    "exclude_by_default": ["furniture", "decorative_props", "unverified_equipment"]
  },
  "adjacency_graph": [
    {
      "from": "city platform",
      "to": "upper pavilion",
      "connection": "stair",
      "confidence": "confirmed"
    },
    {
      "from": "upper pavilion",
      "to": "roof ensemble",
      "connection": "structural_attachment",
      "confidence": "confirmed"
    }
  ],
  "relationships": [
    "The city platform establishes grounded monumentality and axial symmetry; the upper pavilion expresses hierarchical authority through proportion (9 bays × 5 depths = 'Nine-Five' imperial symbolism); the roof ensemble articulates ritual hierarchy via ridge count, color (yellow = imperial), and beast sequence."
  ],
  "spatial_envelope": {
    "mode": "semi_open",
    "footprint": "rectangular, approx. 119 m wide × 33.7 m deep (based on verified width; depth inferred from proportional consistency)",
    "boundary_segments": ["floor", "wall", "roof"],
    "openings": ["arched portal", "linghua window", "eave overhang"],
    "vertical_connections": ["stair ramp", "structural column-to-roof junction"]
  },
  "visual_language": {
    "style": "Chinese imperial architecture, Ming–Qing transitional style",
    "materials": ["vermilion-painted brick and timber", "yellow glazed ceramic roof tiles", "Hanbaiyu (white marble) base and balustrade", "gold-leafed lacquer paint on dougong and beams"],
    "lighting": "clear daylight, frontal sun angle emphasizing relief of dougong, ridge ornaments, and window latticework",
    "mood": "solemn, monumental, ceremonial, historically resonant"
  },
  "must_have": [
    "Vermilion-red wall surfaces with consistent pigment tone and subtle weathering",
    "Double-eaved xieshan roof with correct ridge count (9) and chiwen placement (10 total)",
    "Linghua-pattern windows (36 frontal, diamond-grid with floral infill)",
    "Hanbaiyu balustrade with continuous lotus-and-vase carving",
    "Visible dougong clusters beneath eaves — layered, interlocking wooden brackets with painted details",
    "Yellow glazed roof tiles with directional lay and visible interlocking profile"
  ],
  "quality_gates": [
    "Roof ridge geometry must conform to 'eight eaves, nine ridges' structural logic",
    "No interior room layout or furniture modeling — strictly exterior envelope and surface treatment",
    "All materials must be physically plausible for Blender Cycles/Eevee rendering (PBR textures, normal maps, displacement where appropriate)",
    "Balustrade height and spacing must support human-scale readability (approx. 1.2 m top rail, 0.35 m baluster spacing)"
  ],
  "delivery_views": [
    "Front elevation (full-frame, centered, eye-level at 1.6 m)",
    "3/4 front-right perspective (showing roof slope, corner dougong, and balustrade continuity)",
    "Detail close-up of dougong cluster under eave (with visible 'qiao', 'ang', 'gong' components)",
    "Roof plan view (showing ridge layout and chiwen positions)"
  ],
  "prompt_directives": [
    "Use real-world reference proportions — avoid cartoonish exaggeration of bracket depth or roof pitch",
    "Prioritize material fidelity over geometric perfection: slight irregularities in tile alignment and wood grain acceptable",
    "Render all architectural elements as built assemblies — no floating geometry or disconnected parts",
    "Exclude modern signage, scaffolding, or non-historical infrastructure"
  ],
  "hard_constraints": [
    "No interior spaces modeled — zero floor plans, ceilings, or room volumes beyond envelope shell",
    "No human figures, vehicles, or landscape beyond immediate plinth and outer Golden River bridges",
    "All dimensions must remain relative and scalable — no fixed metric units required",
    "Do not model structural internals (nails, joinery, framing members) unless visually exposed and documented"
  ],
  "soft_constraints": [
    "Prefer historical accuracy over photographic realism — e.g., use traditional pigment-based color palette rather than hyperrealistic weathering",
    "Slight atmospheric haze acceptable to reinforce monumentality and distance",
    "Subtle ambient occlusion on dougong undersides and balustrade joints encouraged"
  ],
  "uncertainties": [
    "Exact tile size and laying pattern (source mentions 'glazed yellow tiles' but not module dimensions)",
    "Precise dougong layer count per bracket set (described as 'layered' and 'ordered' but no count given)",
    "Balustrade height above platform edge (only total platform height and base height provided)",
    "Exact number and arrangement of zodiac beasts beyond '1 immortal + 9 beasts' — order may vary by source"
  ],
  "sources": [
    {
      "title": "详解天安门城楼的建筑特色 - China Daily",
      "url": "https://www.chinadaily.com.cn/dfpd/2009-09/22/content_8720224.htm",
      "channel": "agent_reach_exa",
      "reason": "Primary confirmation of roof type (double-eaved xieshan), dougong description, linghua windows, and color scheme."
    },
    {
      "title": "天安门",
      "url": "https://zh.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E5%A4%A9%E5%AE%89%E9%96%80",
      "channel": "agent_reach_exa",
      "reason": "Confirms platform height (13 m), base height (1.59 m), total height (34.7 m), and five-arch layout."
    },
    {
      "title": "地标建筑 天安门 - 建筑之窗",
      "url": "https://www.jianzhuzhichuang.com/cms/dibiaojianzhu/3609.html",
      "channel": "agent_reach_exa",
      "reason": "Verifies 'nine bays × five depths', 'eight eaves nine ridges', and Hanbaiyu balustrade motif (lotus-and-vase)."
    },
    {
      "title": "Tian An Men 天安门 (259) 360 Panorama | 360Cities",
      "url": "https://www.360cities.net/zh/image/tiananmen-gate259-beijing",
      "channel": "agent_reach_exa",
      "reason": "Provides visual confirmation of facade rhythm, roof silhouette, and balustrade continuity."
    }
  ]
}
